sec: ALF causes, idiosyncratic DILI and Paracetamol stages

items.q: Match each etiology of drug-induced acute liver failure with its geographic epidemiology or mechanism — 1) Paracetamol 2) Rifampicin … A) Idiosyncratic dose-independent toxicity that can occur after a single dose B) Most common cause of acute liver failure in Europe
items.exp: Paracetamol is the most common cause of ALF in Europe ('m/c in Europe'), while Rifampicin is an idiosyncratic reaction that can occur after a single dose. (Book p995)

items.q: What are the maximum daily therapeutic dose and the acute toxic threshold dose for paracetamol (acetaminophen)?
opts: Maximum therapeutic: 4 g/day; Toxic dose: > 7.5 g/day
Maximum therapeutic: 2 g/day; Toxic dose: > 4 g/day
Maximum therapeutic: 6 g/day; Toxic dose: > 12 g/day
Maximum therapeutic: 1 g/day; Toxic dose: > 5 g/day
items.exp: The book specifies for Paracetamol: max dose 4 g/day and toxic dose > 7.5 g/day. (Book p995)

items.q: Which of the following drugs is NOT listed as causing dose-independent (idiosyncratic) Acute Liver Failure?
items.exp: Mushroom toxin is listed under dose-dependent causes along with paracetamol; carbamazepine, PTU, valproate, nitrofurantoin, phenytoin, INH, and single-dose rifampicin are idiosyncratic. (Book p995)

items.q: What is the primary pathophysiological driver of hepatic encephalopathy and seizures in acute liver failure?
opts: Elevated intracranial tension and cerebral edema
items.exp: In ALF, hepatic encephalopathy is due to '↑ ICT & Cerebral edema -> Seizures'. (Book p995)

items.q: Assess the two clinical features of acute liver failure: I Coagulopathy is defined by an INR > 1.5, yet the clinical risk of spontaneous overt bleeding is rare. II Active alcohol consumption decreases overall mortality in acute liver failure.
items.exp: Statement I is true because coagulopathy has INR > 1.5 but bleeding is rare. Statement II is false because alcohol causes '↑ mortality'. (Book p995)

items.q: Fill up: In paracetamol hepatotoxicity, excessive metabolism by cytochrome ______ in Zone 3 hepatocytes generates the toxic metabolite NAPQI.
items.exp: Paracetamol is converted to NAPQI by CYP2E1 in Zone 3 hepatocytes. (Book p995)

items.q: Why does NAPQI cause hepatocellular necrosis in paracetamol poisoning?
opts: Glutathione stores are depleted, leaving NAPQI un-metabolized to covalently bind hepatic proteins
NAPQI directly blocks canalicular MRP-2 excretion of bile salts
NAPQI irreversibly uncouples mitochondrial electron transport at Complex I
NAPQI triggers rapid apoptosis of sinusoidal Kupffer cells
items.exp: Accumulated NAPQI is not metabolized because of depletion in hepatic glutathione stores, leading to hepatotoxicity. (Book p995)

items.q: Match each clinical stage of paracetamol poisoning with its post-ingestion timeline — 1) Stage I 2) Stage II 3) Stage III 4) Stage IV … A) 72–96 hours B) < 24 hours C) > 96 hours D) 24–72 hours
items.exp: Timeline: Stage I is <24 hr, Stage II is 24–72 hr, Stage III is 72–96 hr, and Stage IV is >96 hr. (Book p995)

items.q: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 80 hours after ingesting a large handful of acetaminophen tablets. He is in Stage III toxicity. Which laboratory and clinical features characterise this critical stage?
opts: Hepatic encephalopathy, cerebral edema, bilirubin > 4.5 mg/dL, ATN, hypoglycemia, and lactic acidosis
Mild nausea and vomiting with entirely normal transaminases and normal INR
Isolated right upper quadrant tenderness with AST < 100 U/L and absent jaundice
Complete clinical recovery with normalization of all liver enzymes
items.exp: Stage III (72–96 hrs, which determines survival) features encephalopathy, cerebral edema, coagulopathy, bilirubin > 4.5 mg/dL, ATN, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia, lactic acidosis, and MODS. (Book p995)

items.q: Which stage of paracetamol toxicity is explicitly identified as the stage that 'Determines survival'?
items.exp: Stage III (72–96 hrs) is specifically annotated with '(Determines survival)'. (Book p995)

items.q: Fill up: In Stage III paracetamol toxicity, acute renal failure characteristically arises from ______ complicated by sepsis.
items.exp: The table lists 'ATN (Acute Tubular Necrosis) : sepsis + renal failure' in Stage III. (Book p995)

items.q: What serum bilirubin cut-off is listed as a feature of Stage III paracetamol poisoning?
items.exp: Stage III features explicitly include 'Bilirubin > 4.5 mg/dL'. (Book p995)
